brief: The NDX broke a 4-week losing streak, closing up ~350bps, led by the SOX's +800bps (best week since August), yet both indices stayed below their 200-dmas. The author reads the bounce as cleaner positioning (GS PB data: short covering via macro products) plus intra-market rotation into Defensives, Big Tech and Low Vol, against a tougher macro backdrop: US Financial Conditions hit their tightest in ~18 months after a hotter CPI print, with 10yr yields at 5.15% and oil near $96/brl. NVDA fell to -12% YTD, its worst relative week versus Semis since 2008, fueling debate over how far that bounce can stretch. Market consensus on positioning is unusually thin outside a receptive tilt toward hyperscalers, with live debate over bear-market-bounce versus new bull leg. NVDA reports Tuesday post-close at a 14-day RSI of 24 (lowest since 2019) and 11x NTM P/E, market cap back below $4tn and now matching MSFT's. GS Econ's 2027 outlook: 2.8% global growth as lower energy prices and AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions, with downside risk from Iran escalation, French fiscal deficits, AI capex disappointment, and early signs AI is already weighing on the job market.
